description: Raise any base to any exponent. Get base^exponent instantly with the expanded multiplication shown step by step for integer powers.

faqs.a: An exponent tells you how many times to multiply the base by itself. For example, 2^5 means 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 = 32.
A negative exponent means the reciprocal: base^(-n) = 1 / base^n. So 2^(-3) = 1/8 = 0.125.
Fractional exponents represent roots: x^(1/n) is the n-th root of x, so 9^0.5 = 3. The calculator evaluates these with full floating-point precision.
0^0 is mathematically indeterminate. The calculator follows the common computing convention and returns 1, but notes it as undefined in strict mathematics.

howto: Enter the exponent (whole, negative or fractional).
Read the result instantly, including scientific notation for very large or small values.
For small integer exponents, see the multiplication expanded step by step.
